skill.name: jira-safe
skill.description: Plan and create SAFe-aligned Jira epics, stories, subtasks, workflow transitions, and implementation comments for Jira Cloud projects.
skill.summary: Create SAFe-ready Jira work items and workflow updates with Jira Cloud REST API patterns.

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and key detections are false positives from Markdown formatting, JavaScript template strings, and Jira issue key fields. Real risk remains because executable scripts and skill examples read Jira credentials and make authenticated Jira REST API calls. The main skill also includes a bulk delete helper that can remove project issues without a built-in dry-run guard.

remediation.issue: Jira credentials are read from environment variables and hidden .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Document required variables, validate JIRA_BASE_URL against an approved Atlassian host, and never log authorization headers or tokens.

remediation.issue: A bulk delete helper can delete every matching Jira issue in a project.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the helper from published guidance or require dry-run output, explicit issue allow-lists, and user confirmation before deletion.

remediation.issue: Example scripts can create many Jira issues and subtasks immediately.
remediation.suggestion: Make dry-run mode the default and require confirmation before writing epics, stories, subtasks, comments, or workflow transitions.

content.value_statement: Teams often lose consistency when translating product work into Jira hierarchy. This skill provides SAFe templates, Jira REST patterns, and workflow guidance.
actual_capabilities: Drafts SAFe epic, story, and subtask structures for Jira Cloud.
Explains team-managed and company-managed Jira hierarchy differences.
Formats acceptance criteria with Given-When-Then scenarios.
Provides Jira REST API examples for creating and linking issues.
Includes scripts for creating epics, stories, and subtasks from predefined plans.
Shows workflow transition and comment patterns for Jira issues.
limitations: Requires Jira Cloud credentials and a configured project key.
Examples assume a team-managed SCRUM project unless adapted.
Predefined scripts include product-specific backlog content.
Custom fields must be verified against each Jira instance.

use_cases.title: Plan a SAFe backlog
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into epics, stories, subtasks, acceptance criteria, and definitions of done.

use_cases.title: Create implementation stories
use_cases.description: Prepare Jira stories that link to epics and include clear technical subtasks for delivery work.

use_cases.title: Track work through Jira states
use_cases.description: Move issues through available workflow transitions and add implementation comments after work is complete.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SAFe user story for this feature: [feature]. Include summary, acceptance criteria, and definition of done.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down an Epic
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this initiative into one Jira epic, several stories, and practical subtasks: [initiative]. Use team-managed Jira hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Jira Creation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the Jira creation plan for project [project key]. Show the epic, stories, parent links, labels, and required environment variables.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate Workflow Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: For Jira issue [issue key], plan workflow transitions, implementation comments, and completion checks. Query available transitions before proposing changes.

output_examples.input: Create a story for password reset in a team-managed Jira project.
output_examples.output: A SAFe story with persona, goal, benefit, three acceptance scenarios, definition of done, labels, and a parent epic recommendation.

output_examples.input: Break down a client management epic into delivery work.
output: One epic focused on client management value.
Stories for create, list, update, delete, and ownership checks.
Subtasks covering API routes, validation, tests, and UI states.

output_examples.input: Move SCRUM-148 to Done and add implementation notes.
output_examples.output: A workflow plan that first checks available transitions, then proposes a comment with files changed, commits, validation, and final status.

best_practices: Confirm Jira project type before choosing parent fields or custom fields.
Ask for user approval before creating or changing Jira issues.
Use dry runs for bulk backlog creation or deletion tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not assume custom field IDs are the same across Jira instances.
Do not run predefined scripts against production without reviewing the generated issues.
Do not store Jira API tokens in committed files or shared transcripts.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Jira Cloud?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use Jira Cloud REST API v3 and Atlassian Document Format.

faq.question: Does it support team-managed Jira projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The main guidance focuses on team-managed projects and parent-based issue linking.

faq.question: Can it create Jira issues automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, included scripts can create issues when credentials and project settings are configured.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: The scripts expect a Jira email, API token, base URL, and project key from environment variables.

faq.question: Can it delete Jira issues?
faq.answer: The documentation includes a bulk delete example. Review and gate that pattern before use.

faq.question: Can it validate custom Jira fields?
faq.answer: It shows how to query fields, but each Jira instance must be checked before creating issues.
